entries.test_name: Choices > Move requests > should allow specifying switch targets
Choice parser > Team Preview requests > should accept only `team` choices
entries.detail: Gen 3 OU team preview is not part of the current native request model.

entries.test_name: Choice parser > Switch requests > Doubles/Triples > should accept only `switch` and `pass` choices
Choice parser > Move requests > Generic > should allow mega evolving and targeting in the same move in either order
entries.detail: Mega Evolution does not exist in Generation 3.

entries.test_name: Battle#onEvent > should support and resolve priorities correctly
entries.detail: Dynamic event handler registration belongs to Checkpoint 2; this is not an ordinary action-queue ordering case.

entries.test_name: Accuracy > should chain modifiers in order of the Pokemon's raw speed
entries.detail: Accuracy-modifying event handlers are outside the current supported feature map.

entries.test_name: Fainting > should check for a winner after recoil
entries.detail: Recoil effects are not implemented by the current ordinary-damage slice.

entries.test_name: Quick Claw > [Gen 3] causes Speed ties with every holder when activated
entries.detail: The test depends on Quick Claw item handlers, sleep, and direct mutation of the oracle's quickClawRoll field. Those semantics are outside Checkpoint 1 and the forced outcome is not a portable case input.

entries.test_name: Levitate > should give the user an immunity to Ground-type moves
entries.detail: The literal test uses the default generation and Rotom, which did not exist in Generation 3. Checkpoint 2 uses legal Gen 3 source-linked cases against the same runImmunity/isGrounded boundary.

entries.test_name: Flash Fire [Gen 3-4] > should activate and grant Fire-type immunity even if the user is frozen in Gen 3
entries.detail: The literal test injects frozen status and exercises Gen 3's frozen Flash Fire exception. Status state and persistent Flash Fire activation are outside this checkpoint's bounded handler slice.

entries.test_name: Burn > should halve damage from most Physical attacks
entries.detail: The literal test runs in the default current generation with No Guard and Prankster. Checkpoint 3 uses a legal Gen 3 derived case against the Gen 3 modifyDamage burn boundary.

entries.test_name: Burn > should inflict 1/16 of max HP at the end of the turn, rounded down
entries.detail: Checkpoint 3 supplies burn as explicit initial mutable state and terminates its cases before residuals. Burn acquisition and residual damage remain outside this bounded modifier slice.

entries.test_name: Choice Items > should restore the same Choice lock after dynamax ends
entries.detail: The only generic Choice Item test is a Generation 8 Dynamax interaction. Checkpoint 3 deliberately uses Black Belt instead of partially implementing Choice Band without its lock semantics.

entries.test_name: Toxic Poison > should inflict 1/16 of max HP rounded down, times the number of active turns with the status, at the end of the turn
entries.detail: The literal test runs in the default current generation. Checkpoint 4 preserves it as source evidence and uses a legal Gen 3 derived Toxic ramp case against the inherited status lifecycle.

entries.test_name: Toxic Poison > should reset the damage counter when the Pokemon switches out
entries.detail: The literal test runs in the default current generation and uses Whirlwind. Checkpoint 4 uses an ordinary Gen 3 switch-out and switch-in sequence against the same Toxic SwitchIn reset boundary.

entries.test_name: Weather damage calculation > should wear off on the final turn before weather effects are applied
entries.detail: The literal test uses permanent ability-started Sandstorm in the default generation. Checkpoint 4 instead derives a Gen 3 move-started five-turn Sandstorm case and proves four damage ticks followed by expiry before the fifth tick.
